chapter_theme: Asana (ஆதனம்): of the many postures, a few are named and described, the lotus, the auspicious, the cock and the lion, with svastika as the steady seat in which one becomes master; the closing verse lists the chief seven and counts the postures in the hundreds.
structure_note: An opening verse on the many postures and svastika (558), four descriptions of single postures (559 to 562), and a closing list and count (563).

558.reading: Of the many postures that spread out from the lotus, eight are chief; among them, one who sits firmly in svastika without strain becomes master.
558.nuance: இரு நாலும் (two fours) gives eight. சொங்கு is taken as flaw or strain; தலைவன் may mean master of the posture or of yoga itself. The verse names svastika (சுவத்திகம்) as the seat to settle in, though it then describes others.

559.reading: Setting one foot upon the opposite thigh, drawing the other firmly over it, and laying the hands beautifully upon them: this is called padmasana.
559.nuance: ஓரணையப் பதம் is a compressed phrase, read as one foot set against the other thigh; the hands resting on the feet is one reading of அதனைத்தன் மேல்வைக்க.

560.reading: Placing the right foot clearly over the other, stretching the hands out on the knees and holding the body upright with ease: that is bhadrasana.
560.nuance: உருசியொடு (with relish) suggests the posture is held with ease, not strain. Which foot goes under is implied, not stated.

561.reading: Setting both feet together on the thighs and lifting the body to rest upon the elbows, holding still without wavering: that is the cock posture.
561.nuance: முக்கி (straining) and தொக்க அறிந்து are unclear; the description matches the cock posture of later manuals, where the arms pass through the crossed legs, but the verse doesn't say so.

562.reading: Stretching the hands to the knees over the feet, opening the mouth wide and fixing the clear eyes on the tip of the nose: that is called the lion posture.
562.nuance: The open mouth and the gaze at the nose-tip (கொடிமூக்கு) are the marks of the posture; the placing of the feet is compressed.

563.reading: Bhadra, gomukha, the lotus, the lion, sothiram, vira and sukhasana are the seven best; the postures are many, counted as eight and eight, ten and a hundred.
563.nuance: எட்டெட்டுப் பத்தொடு நூறு is traditionally summed as 126 postures (8 + 8 + 10 + 100), but it can also be read as 64 and 110; I can't fix the count. சொத்திரம் is taken as svastika (சொத்திகம்). The variant மயூரம் would add the peacock posture to the list.

source_issues: 563: a variant reads முத்த மயூரமுது for முத்தம மாமுது, putting the peacock posture (மயூரம்) in the list in place of உத்தமம் (best), which changes what the seven are.
563: சொத்திரம் is not a known posture name; it may be a corruption of சொத்திகம் (svastika), named in 558.
